title: Springfield and Chicago clubs with Oliver Bibbs
summary: After the war Punch worked with Oliver Bibbs in Springfield and at several Chicago clubs.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Forty-one. Well, I was wondering about it, Pontch. Let me fix that machine there. When were you in Springfield? Right.

Well, I was there with a fellow named Oliver Bibbs. That was late after, way after me and Francois and them broke up. That's where I must have been in. It must have been around thirty, oh, not no thirty. Around about, 45 or something like that. 46, 47, around that day. Long after you'd stopped drinking then. Yeah. Oh yeah, I quit drinking altogether.
Was the war going on there? Right after World War II. Right after World War II, I see. I see.
Well, that was a good job. Mm-hmm. That was Sidney Bichet, the fellow that had been playing there, and he went overseas, and we took his place.
Well, let's see. Now, let's see. Sir Oliver Bibbs, how many jobs did you play with him? Play many places with him?

Yeah, I worked Silhouette Club with him, and I worked at Garrick Bar with him, and I worked at Club Rio with him, and I worked at, what was it? Martin's Condor. Martin's Condor. Mm-hmm. On the west side with him. That's in Chicago. Oh yeah. Oh yeah. Oh, Chicago. And that Silhouette Club is a beautiful place. On Harvard Street. Well, when did you first start going on the road then? When I left with Miramac Miramacos. First trip I took.
